Speaking of sound, an audio editor/ import feature would be awesome for animation lip synching while in the Cheetah program, if it's possible in the future one day. 

For now, I have a sound set up where I can do a lip synch in a movie program, then map out all the vowels and timing, then jump into Cheetah to animate each mouth movement frame by frame without actually hearing it of course till I render out the animation, then bring it back into the movie program and it will match perfectly with the audio already there, so long as I carefully follow the chart created. 

More time consuming, so if there is eventually a way to import audio into Cheetah, that would be a very welcome animator feature and really enhance the appeal to animators, considering the animation program is easy to use and get the hang of compared to other programs.

Here is a script in the Wish List under a sound wish, with a .js script that doesn't work, but crashes Cheetah 4.6 and 4.7 each time it's loaded while in Cheetah. This option would import files from a lip synch program without the sound apparently, and automatically translate the mouth's with the morphs into animated key frames that could then be rendered as animation, and brought back into a movie program to be aligned with the audio. 

I can imagine why the script below (IMPORT LIPSYNCH.JS) won't work, but not sure why. Is such a script even possible? If so, it would be of great use, considering there's no audio in Cheetah.
